questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
In an activity, NaOH solution containing phenolphthalein turns colourless when excess dilute HCl is added. When a few drops of NaOH are then added, the pink colour reappears. Consider the following statements:
(i) In the original pink solution, hydroxide ions are present.
(ii) The colourless solution after adding acid may be neutral or acidic.
(iii) The pink colour reappears because NaCl breaks down back into NaOH and HCl.
(iv) The essential reaction in neutralisation is $H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l)$.
Which statements are correct?
options: (i) and (iii) only
(ii) and (iii) only
(i), (ii) and (iv) only
(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NaOH gives OH⁻ ions in water, which make phenolphthalein pink.
(ii) Correct: phenolphthalein is colourless in both neutral and acidic solutions.
(iii) Incorrect: NaCl does not decompose. The added NaOH first neutralises the excess acid, and then makes the solution basic again.
(iv) Correct: in neutralisation, H⁺(aq) and OH⁻(aq) combine to form water.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Even when concentrated sulphuric acid is added slowly to a large volume of water with stirring, the solution becomes warm.
Reason (R): Dilution increases the concentration of hydronium ions per unit volume.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Dissolving the acid in water is always highly exothermic. The safe method only spreads the heat out; it does not stop heat from being released.
R is false. Dilution decreases the hydronium ion concentration per unit volume.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student adds dilute hydrochloric acid slowly to a small amount of black copper oxide in a beaker, stirring all the time. The copper oxide dissolves and the solution turns blue-green. Which substance causes this colour?
options: Copper(II) hydroxide
Copper(II) chloride
Copper(II) sulphate
Unreacted copper oxide
questions.explanation:
Copper oxide is a metal oxide. It reacts with HCl to form a salt and water.
Reaction: $CuO + 2HCl \rightarrow CuCl_2 + H_2O$
The salt formed is copper(II) chloride, which gives the solution its blue-green colour.
Copper sulphate would need sulphuric acid, and no sulphate is present.
Copper hydroxide is not a product here, and black CuO cannot give the solution a colour once it dissolves.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match the natural source in List-I with the acid it contains in List-II.
List-I
A. Tamarind
B. Tomato
C. Sour milk (curd)
D. Vinegar
List-II
(i) Acetic acid
(ii) Oxalic acid
(iii) Lactic acid
(iv) Tartaric acid
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(i)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(iv), D-(i)
questions.explanation:
A. Tamarind contains tartaric acid, so A-(iv).
B. Tomato contains oxalic acid, so B-(ii).
C. Sour milk (curd) contains lactic acid, so C-(iii).
D. Vinegar contains acetic acid, so D-(i).
Option (1) swaps the acids of tamarind and tomato, which is the most common slip.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sodium hydrogencarbonate is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
Reason (R): On heating, sodium hydrogencarbonate decomposes to give sodium carbonate.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NaHCO$_3$ is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
R is true. The reaction is 2NaHCO$_3$ → Na$_2$CO$_3$ + H$_2$O + CO$_2$ on heating.
However, the extinguisher does not work by heating. In it, NaHCO$_3$ reacts with an acid (dilute H$_2$SO$_4$) to release CO$_2$, which puts out the fire.
So R does not explain A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (substance dissolved in water) with List-II (ions produced):
List-I
(A) NaOH
(B) $Mg(OH)_2$
(C) HCl
(D) $CH_3COOH$
List-II
(i) $H_3O^+$ and $Cl^-$
(ii) $Na^+$ and $OH^-$
(iii) $H^+(aq)$ and $CH_3COO^-$
(iv) $Mg^{2+}$ and $2OH^-$
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(iii)
questions.explanation:
A: $NaOH \rightarrow Na^+ + OH^-$, so (ii).
B: $Mg(OH)_2 \rightarrow Mg^{2+} + 2OH^-$, so (iv).
C: $HCl + H_2O \rightarrow H_3O^+ + Cl^-$, so (i).
D: acetic acid gives H+(aq) and the acetate ion $CH_3COO^-$, so (iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A few zinc granules are added to about 5 mL of dilute sulphuric acid in a test tube. Bubbles appear on the surface of the granules. Which gas is evolved?
options: Oxygen
Hydrogen
Carbon dioxide
Sulphur dioxide
questions.explanation:
Zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid: Zn + H$_2$SO$_4$ → ZnSO$_4$ + H$_2$.
The bubbles seen on the zinc granules are hydrogen gas.
Carbon dioxide is given off when acids react with carbonates, not with metals, so option (3) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Each of the following is taken in the beaker of the bulb-and-battery conductivity set-up:
dilute HCl, glucose solution, alcohol solution, dilute $H_2SO_4$, NaOH solution, $Ca(OH)_2$ solution, distilled water.
In how many cases will the bulb glow?
questions.explanation:
Dilute HCl and dilute $H_2SO_4$ give H+(aq) ions, so they conduct.
NaOH and $Ca(OH)_2$ solutions give $OH^-$ ions, so they conduct.
Glucose and alcohol solutions do not produce ions, so the bulb does not glow.
Distilled water does not conduct either, because it lacks dissolved ions.
Total = 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the reactions of sodium carbonate and sodium hydrogencarbonate with dilute HCl is INCORRECT?
options: One formula unit of Na$_2$CO$_3$ needs two molecules of HCl for complete reaction
NaHCO$_3$ reacts with HCl in a 1 : 1 ratio
Sodium chloride is the salt formed in both reactions
The gas evolved in both reactions helps a burning candle burn more brightly
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Na$_2$CO$_3$ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H$_2$O + CO$_2$.
(2) Correct: NaHCO$_3$ + HCl → NaCl + H$_2$O + CO$_2$.
(3) Correct: NaCl is the salt formed in both reactions.
(4) Incorrect: CO$_2$ does not support combustion. It puts out a flame, which is why it is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Arrange the following salts in decreasing order of the number of water molecules of crystallisation per formula unit:
P: Plaster of Paris
Q: Hydrated copper sulphate
R: Washing soda
S: Gypsum
options: R > Q > S > P
Q > R > S > P
R > S > Q > P
Q > S > R > P
questions.explanation:
Washing soda is $Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O$, so it has 10 water molecules.
Hydrated copper sulphate is $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$, so it has 5.
Gypsum is $CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$, so it has 2.
Plaster of Paris is $CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$, so it has ½.
The decreasing order is therefore 10 > 5 > 2 > ½, which gives R > Q > S > P.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
A student heats solid sodium chloride with concentrated sulphuric acid in a test tube fitted with a delivery tube. Because the weather is humid, the gas is first passed through a guard tube containing calcium chloride. Consider these statements:
(i) The gas coming out of the delivery tube is hydrogen chloride.
(ii) The gas turns wet blue litmus paper red.
(iii) The gas turns dry blue litmus paper red.
(iv) Calcium chloride in the guard tube absorbs moisture and keeps the gas dry.
Which of the statements are correct?
options: (i), (ii) and (iv) only
(i), (iii) and (iv) only
(ii) and (iii) only
(i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NaCl reacts with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ and gives off HCl gas.
(ii) Correct: on wet litmus, water lets HCl form H$_3$O$^+$ ions, so blue litmus turns red.
(iii) Incorrect: dry HCl forms no H$^+$ ions, so dry litmus does not change colour.
(iv) Correct: CaCl$_2$ acts as a drying agent and removes moisture from the gas.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about pH in everyday life:
I. Quick lime, slaked lime and chalk can all be used to treat an over-acidic field, because each of them neutralises acid.
II. Since our body works within the pH range 7.0 to 7.8, body fluids in this range are slightly acidic.
III. Life as we know it is unlikely on Venus, because its atmosphere has thick clouds of sulphuric acid and living organisms survive only within a narrow pH range.
IV. The stomach normally produces hydrochloric acid to help digestion, and antacids give relief only when this acid is produced in excess.
Which of the statements are correct?
options: I and II only
I, III and IV only
II and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation:
I Correct: calcium oxide is a basic oxide and calcium hydroxide is a base. Calcium carbonate reacts with acid to give salt, CO2 and water. All three reduce soil acidity.
II Incorrect: pH above 7 is basic, so the range 7.0–7.8 is neutral to slightly basic, not acidic.
III Correct: sulphuric acid clouds would give a very low pH, far outside the narrow range organisms can tolerate.
IV Correct: HCl aids digestion without harming the stomach. Excess acid causes pain, and antacids neutralise this excess.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Copper oxide is added to dilute hydrochloric acid with stirring. The copper oxide dissolves and the solution turns blue-green. The blue-green colour is due to the formation of:
options: Copper(II) hydroxide
Copper(II) sulphate
Copper(II) chloride
Hydrogen gas dissolved in water
questions.explanation:
The reaction is CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O.
NCERT states that the blue-green colour comes from the copper(II) chloride formed.
Copper sulphate could not form, because no sulphate ions are present.
Metal oxides react with acids to give a salt and water, not hydrogen gas.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Copper oxide is classified as a basic oxide.
Reason (R): Metallic oxides react with acids to form a salt and water, just as bases do.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. CuO dissolves in dilute HCl and forms CuCl2 and water.
R is true. The general reaction is Metal oxide + Acid → Salt + Water.
This reaction resembles the reaction of a base with an acid. That is exactly why metallic oxides are called basic oxides, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following are uses of washing soda ($Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O$)?
(i) Manufacture of glass
(ii) Making cakes soft and spongy
(iii) Manufacture of borax
(iv) Removing permanent hardness of water
(v) Neutralising excess acid in the stomach as an antacid
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: washing soda is used in the glass, soap and paper industries.
(ii) Incorrect: this is a use of baking powder, whose baking soda releases $CO_2$.
(iii) Correct: washing soda is used to make sodium compounds such as borax.
(iv) Correct: it removes permanent hardness of water.
(v) Incorrect: the antacid ingredient is sodium hydrogencarbonate, not washing soda.
So 3 of the listed items are uses of washing soda.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student uses universal indicator paper instead of litmus paper to test a solution. Which description of universal indicator is correct?
options: A purple dye extracted from lichen that turns red in acids and blue in bases
A mixture of several indicators that shows different colours at different concentrations of hydrogen ions
A substance whose odour changes in acidic or basic medium
A synthetic indicator that is colourless in acids and pink in bases
questions.explanation:
Universal indicator is a mixture of several indicators.
It shows different colours at different H$^+$ ion concentrations, so it tells us roughly how acidic or basic a solution is, not just whether it is an acid or a base.
Option (1) describes litmus. Option (3) describes olfactory indicators such as onion or clove oil. Option (4) describes phenolphthalein.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: After a sugary meal, the pH in the mouth may fall below 5.5. This happens because bacteria degrade the sugar and food particles to produce acids, and the tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) then gets corroded even though it does not dissolve in water.
Statement II: Toothpastes are generally acidic, which helps them dissolve away the food particles and stop tooth decay.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Bacteria in the mouth produce acids from leftover sugar and food. Tooth decay starts when the mouth pH falls below 5.5. Enamel, made of calcium hydroxyapatite (a crystalline calcium phosphate), is insoluble in water but is corroded in such acidic conditions.
Statement II is incorrect. Toothpastes are generally basic, not acidic. They neutralise the excess acid in the mouth and so prevent decay. An acidic paste would lower the pH further and worsen corrosion.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Plaster of Paris should be stored in a moisture-proof container.
Statement II: Plaster of Paris reacts with water to change back into gypsum, which is a hard solid mass.
options: Both statements are true, and Statement II correctly explains Statement I.
Both statements are true, but Statement II does not explain Statement I.
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. Plaster of Paris is always kept away from moisture.
Statement II is true: $CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O \rightarrow CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$ (gypsum, a hard mass).
If moisture from the air reached the powder, it would slowly set and become useless. This is exactly why it must be stored in a moisture-proof container, so II explains I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Hydrogen ions released by an acid in water cannot exist alone. In which form are they present in an aqueous solution?
options: As free protons, H$^+$
As hydroxide ions, OH$^-$
As hydronium ions, H$_3$O$^+$
As hydrogen gas, H$_2$
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that H$^+$ ions cannot exist alone. They combine with water molecules: H$^+$ + H$_2$O → H$_3$O$^+$.
So they must be shown as H$^+$(aq) or as the hydronium ion, H$_3$O$^+$.
Option (1) is tempting, but a free H$^+$ does not stay separate in water.
OH$^-$ comes from bases, and H$_2$ gas forms only when an acid reacts with a metal.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Within which pH range does the human body work?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that our body works within the pH range 7.0 to 7.8, which is slightly basic.
Living organisms can survive only within a narrow range of pH change.
The value 5.5 is the pH below which tooth decay starts, not the body's working range.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student takes 2 mL of dilute NaOH solution in a test tube and adds two drops of phenolphthalein. She then adds dilute HCl drop by drop until the acid is in excess. What colour change does she observe?
options: Colourless to pink
Pink to colourless
Blue to red
Pink to blue-green
questions.explanation:
Phenolphthalein turns pink in a basic solution, so the NaOH solution first becomes pink.
As HCl is added, the acid neutralises the base: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O.
Once all the base is used up, phenolphthalein becomes colourless.
Option (1) is the reverse change. Blue to red is the change seen with blue litmus, not phenolphthalein.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In the chlor-alkali process, electricity is passed through brine. Which option correctly states where each product is obtained?
options: Chlorine at the cathode; hydrogen at the anode; sodium hydroxide near the anode
Chlorine at the anode; hydrogen at the cathode; sodium hydroxide near the cathode
Chlorine at the anode; hydrogen at the cathode; sodium hydroxide near the anode
Hydrogen and chlorine both at the anode; sodium hydroxide near the cathode
questions.explanation:
The overall reaction is $2NaCl + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2NaOH + Cl_2 + H_2$.
NCERT states that chlorine is given off at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.
Sodium hydroxide solution forms near the cathode.
Option (3) has the correct gases but places NaOH at the wrong electrode.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a use of washing soda and NOT of baking soda?
options: As an ingredient in antacids
In soda-acid fire extinguishers
For removing permanent hardness of water
For making cakes soft and spongy
questions.explanation:
Washing soda (Na$_2$CO$_3$·10H$_2$O) is used to remove permanent hardness of water. It is also used in the glass, soap and paper industries.
The other three options are all uses of baking soda (NaHCO$_3$): antacids, fire extinguishers and baking powder.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: HCl gas is prepared by adding concentrated sulphuric acid to solid sodium chloride. On a humid day, the gas is passed through a guard tube containing calcium chloride before it is tested with blue litmus. Why is the guard tube used?
options: To convert NaCl into HCl
To dry the HCl gas by absorbing moisture
To neutralise excess sulphuric acid vapours
To dissolve the HCl gas in water
questions.explanation:
Calcium chloride is a drying agent. It absorbs water vapour from the gas.
The aim is to test truly dry HCl gas, so moisture must be removed.
The guard tube does not produce HCl (option 1), neutralise acid (option 3) or dissolve the gas (option 4).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Two drops of phenolphthalein are added to 2 mL of dilute NaOH solution. Dilute HCl is then added drop by drop until the colour just disappears. After that, a few drops of NaOH are added again. Which option correctly describes the changes in colour and pH?
options: The pink colour disappears as the pH rises above 7; it reappears when NaOH lowers the pH again
The pink colour disappears as the pH falls from above 7 to about 7 or below; it reappears because added NaOH raises the pH above 7 again
The pink colour disappears as the pH falls; it cannot reappear because the NaCl formed is an acidic salt
The colour changes only because of dilution; the pH stays at 7 throughout because NaCl is neutral
questions.explanation:
Phenolphthalein is pink in basic solution, so NaOH (pH above 7) turns it pink.
Adding HCl neutralises the base: H$^+$(aq) + OH$^-$(aq) → H$_2$O. The pH falls to about 7, and the pink colour vanishes.
NaCl is a salt of a strong acid and a strong base, so it is neutral, not acidic. This rules out option (3).
Extra NaOH supplies OH$^-$ ions again. The pH rises above 7, and the pink colour returns.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Electricity is passed through brine in the chlor-alkali process. How many of the following statements about this process are correct?
(i) Chlorine gas is given off at the anode.
(ii) Hydrogen gas is given off at the cathode.
(iii) Sodium hydroxide solution is formed near the anode.
(iv) Brine is an aqueous solution of sodium chloride.
(v) All three products of the process are useful.
questions.explanation:
The reaction is 2NaCl(aq) + 2H$_2$O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl$_2$(g) + H$_2$(g).
(i) Correct: Cl$_2$ is released at the anode.
(ii) Correct: H$_2$ is released at the cathode.
(iii) Incorrect: NaOH forms near the cathode, not the anode.
(iv) Correct: brine is aqueous NaCl.
(v) Correct: NCERT notes that all three products are useful.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following reactions give only a salt and water as products?
(i) $NaOH + HCl$
(ii) $CuO + 2HCl$
(iii) $Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2$
(iv) $Zn + H_2SO_4$
(v) $Na_2CO_3 + 2HCl$
questions.explanation:
(i) Gives NaCl + H2O, which is only a salt and water.
(ii) Gives CuCl2 + H2O, which is only a salt and water.
(iii) Gives CaCO3 + H2O, which is only a salt and water.
(iv) Gives ZnSO4 + H2. Hydrogen gas is formed instead of water.
(v) Gives 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. Carbon dioxide is formed as well.
So three reactions qualify.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student adds a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid to 10 mL of water in a beaker, swirls it gently, and touches the base of the beaker. What will the student notice, and what type of process is this?
options: The beaker feels cold; the process is endothermic
The beaker feels warm; the process is exothermic
There is no change in temperature; no heat is involved
The beaker feels cold; the process is exothermic
questions.explanation:
Dissolving a concentrated acid in water releases a large amount of heat.
Because heat is given out, the beaker becomes warm, so the process is exothermic.
An endothermic process absorbs heat and would make the beaker feel cold, so (1) is wrong.
Option (4) is self-contradictory, because an exothermic process cannot make the beaker cold.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Washing soda is obtained by recrystallisation of sodium carbonate.
Statement II: The chemical formula of washing soda is $Na_2CO_3 \cdot 5H_2O$.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I: Correct. Heating baking soda gives sodium carbonate. Recrystallising sodium carbonate gives washing soda: $Na_2CO_3 + 10H_2O \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O$.
Statement II: Incorrect. Washing soda has ten water molecules of crystallisation, not five. Five water molecules are found in hydrated copper sulphate, $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following salts give an aqueous solution with pH more than 7?
Sodium chloride, potassium nitrate, aluminium chloride, zinc sulphate, sodium acetate, sodium carbonate, sodium hydrogencarbonate
questions.explanation:
A salt of a strong base and a weak acid is basic, with pH > 7.
Three salts qualify: sodium acetate (from acetic acid), sodium carbonate and sodium hydrogencarbonate (both from carbonic acid). Each comes from NaOH and a weak acid.
NaCl and KNO$_3$ come from a strong acid and a strong base, so they are neutral (pH 7).
AlCl$_3$ and ZnSO$_4$ come from a strong acid and a weak base, so they are acidic.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match the natural source in List-I with the acid present in it in List-II.
List-I: (P) Tamarind (Q) Tomato (R) Curd (S) Vinegar
List-II: (i) Lactic acid (ii) Acetic acid (iii) Tartaric acid (iv) Oxalic acid
options: P-(iii), Q-(iv), R-(i), S-(ii)
P-(iv), Q-(iii), R-(i), S-(ii)
P-(iii), Q-(iv), R-(ii), S-(i)
P-(ii), Q-(iv), R-(i), S-(iii)
questions.explanation:
Use Table 2.3 to match each source:
Tamarind contains tartaric acid, so P-(iii).
Tomato contains oxalic acid, so Q-(iv).
Sour milk (curd) contains lactic acid, so R-(i).
Vinegar contains acetic acid, so S-(ii).
Option (2) swaps tamarind and tomato, which is a common mix-up.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Aqueous solutions of the following salts are tested with pH paper:
Sodium chloride, potassium nitrate, aluminium chloride, zinc sulphate, copper sulphate, sodium acetate, sodium carbonate, sodium hydrogencarbonate
How many of these solutions will have a pH less than 7?
questions.explanation:
A salt of a strong acid and a weak base is acidic (pH < 7).
Aluminium chloride, zinc sulphate and copper sulphate are of this type, which makes 3.
NaCl and KNO3 come from a strong acid and a strong base, so they are neutral (pH = 7).
Sodium acetate, sodium carbonate and sodium hydrogencarbonate come from a strong base and a weak acid, so they are basic (pH > 7).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs correctly match a problem with a suitable remedy as described in NCERT?
(i) Honey-bee sting – baking soda applied on the area
(ii) Nettle sting – rubbing with a dock leaf
(iii) Indigestion due to excess stomach acid – milk of magnesia
(iv) Highly acidic soil – treatment with slaked lime
(v) Ant sting – applying vinegar
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: a bee sting leaves an acid, and baking soda is a mild base that neutralises it.
(ii) Correct: a dock leaf is the traditional remedy that counters the methanoic acid injected by nettle hairs.
(iii) Correct: magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is a mild base used as an antacid.
(iv) Correct: slaked lime is a base that reduces soil acidity.
(v) Incorrect: an ant sting contains methanoic acid, and vinegar is itself acidic (acetic acid), so it cannot neutralise the sting.
So four pairs are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In a chlor-alkali plant, 117 g of sodium chloride in brine is completely electrolysed according to $2NaCl + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2NaOH + Cl_2 + H_2$. What mass of sodium hydroxide is formed? (Molar masses: NaCl = 58.5 g/mol, NaOH = 40 g/mol)
questions.explanation:
Given: mass of NaCl = 117 g, molar mass = 58.5 g/mol.
Moles of NaCl = 117 / 58.5 = 2 mol.
From the equation, 2 mol NaCl gives 2 mol NaOH.
Mass of NaOH = 2 × 40 = 80 g.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Large deposits of solid sodium chloride found in several parts of the world often appear brown. Which statement about this rock salt is correct?
options: It is brown because it contains copper sulphate crystals.
It is brown due to impurities, and it formed when seas of bygone ages dried up.
It is formed by electrolysis of brine in the Earth's crust.
It is brown because it is hydrated sodium chloride.
questions.explanation:
NCERT says rock salt occurs as large crystals that are often brown due to impurities.
Beds of rock salt formed when ancient seas dried up, and the salt is mined like coal.
The other options give causes (copper sulphate, electrolysis, hydration) that NCERT does not mention.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following can be used as olfactory indicators?
Onion, vanilla essence, clove oil, litmus, phenolphthalein, turmeric
questions.explanation:
Olfactory indicators are substances whose odour changes in an acidic or basic medium.
Onion, vanilla essence and clove oil are olfactory indicators, which makes 3.
Litmus and turmeric are natural indicators that change colour, not odour.
Phenolphthalein is a synthetic indicator that also changes colour.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student heats 16.8 g of pure baking soda until it decomposes completely according to 2NaHCO$_3$ → Na$_2$CO$_3$ + H$_2$O + CO$_2$. What mass of sodium carbonate is left? (Atomic masses: Na = 23 u, H = 1 u, C = 12 u, O = 16 u)
questions.explanation:
Given: mass of NaHCO$_3$ = 16.8 g. Molar mass of NaHCO$_3$ = 84 g/mol and of Na$_2$CO$_3$ = 106 g/mol.
Formula: 2 mol NaHCO$_3$ give 1 mol Na$_2$CO$_3$, so 168 g gives 106 g.
Substituting: moles of NaHCO$_3$ = 16.8 ÷ 84 = 0.2 mol, which gives 0.1 mol Na$_2$CO$_3$.
So mass of Na$_2$CO$_3$ = 0.1 × 106 = 10.6 g.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
(ii) Tamarind contains oxalic acid.
(iii) Curd contains lactic acid.
(iv) Both orange and lemon contain citric acid.
(v) An ant sting contains acetic acid.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: our body works within the pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
(ii) Incorrect: tamarind contains tartaric acid. Oxalic acid is found in tomato.
(iii) Correct: sour milk (curd) contains lactic acid.
(iv) Correct: orange and lemon both contain citric acid.
(v) Incorrect: an ant sting contains methanoic acid.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Plaster of Paris should be stored in a moisture-proof container.
Reason (R): In Plaster of Paris, $CaSO_4.\frac{1}{2}H_2O$, two formula units of calcium sulphate share one molecule of water.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: Plaster of Paris absorbs moisture and sets into gypsum, a hard mass, so it must be kept away from moisture.
R is true: half a water molecule is written because two formula units share one water molecule.
However, R only explains the formula. The real reason for A is the reaction $CaSO_4.\frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O \rightarrow CaSO_4.2H_2O$. So R does not explain A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Carbon dioxide is an acidic oxide.
Reason (R): Carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide, a base, to form a salt and water.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
R is true: $Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 + H_2O$. Calcium carbonate is the salt formed, along with water.
A is true: CO2 is the oxide of a non-metal.
A base reacting to give a salt and water is how an acid behaves in neutralisation. So CO2 behaves like an acid.
This is exactly why NCERT concludes that non-metallic oxides are acidic. R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Bleaching powder is manufactured by the action of chlorine on:
options: dry slaked lime, $Ca(OH)_2$
lime water, aqueous $Ca(OH)_2$
limestone, $CaCO_3$
quick lime, $CaO$, dissolved in water
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that bleaching powder is produced by the action of chlorine on dry slaked lime $[Ca(OH)_2]$.
The key word is 'dry'. Lime water is an aqueous solution, so option (2) is incorrect.
Limestone ($CaCO_3$) is a different compound altogether.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A farmer shakes 2 g of soil with 5 mL water, filters it, and tests the filtrate with universal indicator paper. The pH is found to be about 5, which is unsuitable for his crop. Which substance should he add to the field to correct the soil pH?
options: Ammonium chloride
Chalk (calcium carbonate)
Dilute lemon juice
Sodium chloride
questions.explanation:
A pH of about 5 means the soil is acidic, so a base or basic substance is needed to raise the pH.
Chalk (calcium carbonate) reacts with acids, as do quick lime and slaked lime. It neutralises the excess acidity.
Ammonium chloride is a salt of a strong acid and a weak base, so it is acidic. Lemon juice is acidic. Sodium chloride is neutral and cannot change the pH.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Two acid solutions X and Y are prepared with the SAME molar concentration. With universal indicator, X shows pH 1 and Y shows pH 3. Equal lengths of magnesium ribbon are then dropped into equal volumes of each. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Both acids are equally strong because their concentrations are the same, so fizzing is equally vigorous in both.
Y has the higher H$^+$ ion concentration, so fizzing is more vigorous in Y.
X produces more H$^+$ ions, so X is the stronger acid and fizzing is more vigorous in X; X could be HCl and Y could be acetic acid.
X is the weaker acid because a lower pH means fewer H$^+$ ions, so Y could be HCl.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: A lower pH means a higher H$^+$ concentration, so X (pH 1) has more H$^+$ than Y (pH 3).
Step 2: Acid strength depends on the number of H$^+$ ions produced, not on molar concentration. At equal concentration, X is therefore the stronger acid.
Step 3: More H$^+$ means a faster reaction with Mg, so hydrogen fizzing is more vigorous in X.
Step 4: HCl is a strong acid and acetic acid is weak, which fits X and Y. Option (1) wrongly treats concentration as strength.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: When granulated zinc is warmed with sodium hydroxide solution, hydrogen gas is evolved along with a salt. What is the name of this salt?
options: Sodium zincate
Zinc hydroxide
Sodium oxide
Zinc sulphate
questions.explanation:
The reaction is 2NaOH(aq) + Zn(s) → Na$_2$ZnO$_2$(s) + H$_2$(g).
Na$_2$ZnO$_2$ is called sodium zincate.
Zinc sulphate forms only when zinc reacts with sulphuric acid. No sulphate is present in this reaction.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Zinc granules are treated separately with dilute sulphuric acid and with warm sodium hydroxide solution. Consider the following statements:
(i) Hydrogen gas is evolved in both cases.
(ii) With NaOH, the salt formed is sodium zincate, $Na_2ZnO_2$.
(iii) The gas evolved in both cases burns with a pop sound near a burning candle.
(iv) Every metal reacts with sodium hydroxide in the same way to give hydrogen.
(v) In the salt formed with NaOH, the negative ion is made up of the metal and oxygen.
How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: an acid or a base reacting with zinc gives $H_2$.
(ii) Correct: $2NaOH + Zn \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2$.
(iii) Correct: hydrogen-filled bubbles burn with a pop sound.
(iv) Incorrect: NCERT says such reactions are not possible with all metals.
(v) Correct: the zincate ion contains zinc and oxygen.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Brushing teeth with toothpaste after eating helps prevent tooth decay.
Reason (R): Tooth enamel dissolves readily in water, so food particles must be washed away quickly.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. Bacteria in the mouth break down leftover sugar and food particles and produce acids.
Toothpastes are generally basic, so they neutralise this excess acid and help prevent decay.
R is false. Enamel is made of calcium hydroxyapatite, the hardest substance in the body. It does not dissolve in water.
Enamel is only corroded when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Case: A student prepared HCl gas from solid NaCl and concentrated $H_2SO_4$ on a very humid day. She did not use a calcium chloride guard tube. She was surprised that the 'dry' blue litmus paper also slowly turned red. Which is the most appropriate explanation?
options: HCl gas is acidic even when no water is present.
Moisture from the humid air let HCl form $H_3O^+$ ions on the litmus paper.
Solid NaCl is acidic and its particles reached the litmus paper.
The litmus paper was turned red by $OH^-$ ions formed in the gas.
questions.explanation:
Pure dry HCl gas cannot release H+ ions, so it should not affect dry litmus.
Without a drying agent on a humid day, water vapour is present in the gas and air.
This water lets HCl ionise: $HCl + H_2O \rightarrow H_3O^+ + Cl^-$. The litmus then turns red.
Option (1) contradicts NCERT. NaCl is neutral, and $OH^-$ ions turn red litmus blue, not blue litmus red.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A black powder X dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid and gives a blue-green solution with no gas evolved. A colourless gas Y, obtained by burning charcoal, turns lime water milky, and the milkiness disappears when Y is passed in excess. Which conclusion is correct?
options: X is copper oxide, an acidic oxide; Y is carbon dioxide, a basic oxide
X is copper oxide, a basic oxide; Y is carbon dioxide, an acidic oxide, and the milkiness disappears because soluble $Ca(HCO_3)_2$ forms
X is copper chloride; Y is hydrogen, and the milkiness disappears because $CaCO_3$ decomposes
X is copper oxide, a basic oxide; Y is carbon dioxide, and the milkiness disappears because $Ca(OH)_2$ is formed again
questions.explanation:
X: a black powder that gives a blue-green solution (CuCl2) and water with HCl is CuO. Metal oxide + acid → salt + water, so X is a basic oxide.
Y: burning charcoal gives CO2, which forms a CaCO3 precipitate with base Ca(OH)2. A non-metal oxide reacting with a base makes CO2 acidic.
In excess, CaCO3 + H2O + CO2 → Ca(HCO3)2, which is soluble, so the milkiness clears. Ca(OH)2 is not formed again.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Rain water is called acid rain when its pH falls below which value?
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines acid rain as rain water with a pH less than 5.6.
When acid rain flows into rivers, it lowers the pH of the river water and makes survival difficult for aquatic life.
5.5 is a tempting option, but it is the pH below which tooth decay starts, not the limit for acid rain.
7.0 is the pH of a neutral solution, and 7.0–7.8 is the range in which our body works.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a neutralisation reaction?
options: $Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2$
$2NaOH + Zn \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2$
$CaCO_3 + H_2O + CO_2 \rightarrow Ca(HCO_3)_2$
$NaOH + HCl \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O$
questions.explanation:
A neutralisation reaction is one in which an acid and a base react to give a salt and water.
Option (4): the base NaOH reacts with the acid HCl to give the salt NaCl and water. This is neutralisation.
Options (1) and (2) are reactions of a metal with an acid or a base. They give hydrogen gas, not water.
Option (3) forms soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate. It is not an acid–base reaction.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student adds dilute hydrochloric acid to sodium carbonate taken in a test tube. She passes the gas evolved through lime water, and the lime water turns milky. The milkiness is due to the formation of:
options: Calcium carbonate
Calcium hydrogencarbonate
Calcium chloride
Calcium oxide
questions.explanation:
Sodium carbonate reacts with HCl to give NaCl, water and CO$_2$ gas.
Lime water is calcium hydroxide solution. It reacts with CO$_2$: Ca(OH)$_2$ + CO$_2$ → CaCO$_3$ + H$_2$O.
CaCO$_3$ is insoluble in water, so it forms a white precipitate that makes the solution look milky.
Calcium hydrogencarbonate is soluble, so it cannot cause milkiness. It forms only when CO$_2$ is passed in excess.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The thick white and yellowish clouds in the atmosphere of the planet Venus are made up of which substance?
options: Hydrochloric acid
Sulphuric acid
Nitric acid
Carbonic acid
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the atmosphere of Venus is made up of thick white and yellowish clouds of sulphuric acid.
This strongly acidic environment makes it unlikely that life as we know it can exist there.
Hydrochloric acid is the tempting option because it is the acid in our stomach, but it does not form the Venus clouds.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A solution of hydrochloric acid is mixed with a large volume of water. Which statement correctly describes the change?
options: The concentration of $H_3O^+$ ions per unit volume increases
The concentration of $H_3O^+$ ions per unit volume decreases
All the $H_3O^+$ ions are converted into $OH^-$ ions
The concentration of $H_3O^+$ ions per unit volume stays the same
questions.explanation:
Mixing an acid with water spreads the same $H_3O^+$ ions over a larger volume.
So the number of $H_3O^+$ ions in each unit volume falls. This process is called dilution.
Water does not neutralise the acid, so the ions are not turned into $OH^-$, and (3) is wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): While diluting concentrated sulphuric acid, the acid should be added slowly to water with constant stirring.
Reason (R): Dissolving a concentrated acid in water is a highly exothermic process.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT advises adding the acid slowly to water with constant stirring, never water to the acid.
R is true: mixing a concentrated acid with water releases a lot of heat.
If water is added to the acid, this heat can make the mixture splash out and cause burns, or break the glass by local heating. So R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Plaster of Paris is written as $CaSO_4.\frac{1}{2}H_2O$. When it is mixed with water, it sets into gypsum. How many water molecules are needed to convert two formula units of Plaster of Paris completely into gypsum?
questions.explanation:
The half water molecule means that two formula units of $CaSO_4$ share one water molecule. So two units of Plaster of Paris contain 1 water molecule in total.
Gypsum is $CaSO_4.2H_2O$. Two formula units of gypsum need $2 \times 2 = 4$ water molecules.
Water to be added = 4 − 1 = 3 molecules.
This matches the equation $CaSO_4.\frac{1}{2}H_2O + 1\frac{1}{2}H_2O \rightarrow CaSO_4.2H_2O$, doubled.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Adding concentrated acid slowly to water with stirring
(b) Adding water to concentrated acid
(c) Mixing a base solution with more water
(d) Distilled water placed between the nails in a bulb circuit
List-II
(i) Bulb does not glow
(ii) Heat spreads safely through the water
(iii) Mixture splashes, causing burns
(iv) $OH^-$ concentration per unit volume decreases
options: a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv
a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i
questions.explanation:
(a)-(ii): adding acid slowly to a large volume of water lets the heat spread safely.
(b)-(iii): adding water to the acid releases heat in one spot, and the mixture splashes.
(c)-(iv): diluting a base lowers the $OH^-$ ions per unit volume.
(d)-(i): distilled water has almost no ions, so the bulb does not glow.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following substances will release carbon dioxide when treated with dilute hydrochloric acid?
Marble chips, chalk, baking soda, washing soda, zinc granules, common salt, limestone, quick lime (CaO)
questions.explanation:
Marble, chalk and limestone (all CaCO$_3$), baking soda (NaHCO$_3$) and washing soda (Na$_2$CO$_3$·10H$_2$O) are carbonates or hydrogencarbonates. All five give CO$_2$.
Zinc granules give hydrogen gas, not CO$_2$.
Common salt (NaCl) does not react to give any gas.
Quick lime is a metal oxide, so it gives only a salt and water.
Total = 5.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Blue crystals of hydrated copper sulphate are heated in a dry boiling tube. What colour does the residue become?
options: White
Deep blue
Green
Black
questions.explanation:
Hydrated copper sulphate, $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$, is blue because of its water of crystallisation.
On heating, this water is driven off and anhydrous $CuSO_4$ is left behind. Anhydrous copper sulphate is white.
The colour does not deepen to a darker blue, because the water responsible for the blue colour is lost.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following statements about salts is INCORRECT?
options: $NH_4Cl$ solution is acidic because it is formed from a strong acid and a weak base.
Solutions of both $Na_2CO_3$ and $NaHCO_3$ turn red litmus blue.
$CuSO_4$ and $K_2SO_4$ belong to the sulphate family, so their aqueous solutions have the same pH.
The salt formed by neutralising $HNO_3$ with $NaOH$ gives a solution of pH about 7.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: $HCl$ is a strong acid and $NH_4OH$ is a weak base, so $NH_4Cl$ is acidic.
(2) Correct: both salts come from $NaOH$ and a weak acid, so both are basic.
(3) Incorrect: the two salts share the sulphate radical, but their bases differ. $Cu(OH)_2$ is weak, so $CuSO_4$ has pH < 7. $KOH$ is strong, so $K_2SO_4$ has pH about 7.
(4) Correct: $NaNO_3$ is a strong acid–strong base salt, so it is neutral.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda and a weak edible acid. Which acid is it?
options: Acetic acid
Citric acid
Tartaric acid
Lactic acid
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes baking powder as sodium hydrogencarbonate mixed with tartaric acid, which is a weak edible acid.
When baking powder is heated or wetted, the acid reacts with NaHCO$_3$ and releases CO$_2$.
Citric acid and acetic acid are also edible acids, but they are not the stated component of baking powder.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the chlor-alkali process, chlorine gas is liberated at the cathode.
Reason (R): Hydrogen gas is liberated at the cathode during electrolysis of brine.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is false: chlorine is liberated at the anode, not the cathode.
R is true: hydrogen gas is given off at the cathode, and NaOH forms near the cathode.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: At what temperature does gypsum lose part of its water of crystallisation to form Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that gypsum, $CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$, is heated at 373 K to form Plaster of Paris.
At this temperature it loses water and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate, $CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$.
The value 373 K is the same as 100 °C. 273 K (0 °C) is far too low to drive off water.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Litmus solution is a purple dye extracted from lichen, a plant belonging to the division Thallophyta.
Statement II: Turmeric is a synthetic acid-base indicator, like methyl orange.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: litmus is a purple dye obtained from lichen (Thallophyta). It stays purple in a solution that is neither acidic nor basic.
Statement II is incorrect: turmeric is a natural indicator. Methyl orange and phenolphthalein are the synthetic indicators named in NCERT.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match List-I (experiment) with List-II (observation).
List-I:
(a) Phenolphthalein added to dilute NaOH solution
(b) Copper oxide stirred with dilute HCl
(c) Carbon dioxide passed through lime water
(d) Zinc granules added to dilute H2SO4
List-II:
(i) Solution turns blue-green
(ii) Solution turns pink
(iii) White precipitate appears
(iv) Gas evolved burns with a pop sound
options: a-(ii), b-(i), c-(iii), d-(iv)
a-(i), b-(ii), c-(iii), d-(iv)
a-(ii), b-(iii), c-(i), d-(iv)
a-(iv), b-(i), c-(iii), d-(ii)
questions.explanation:
(a) Phenolphthalein turns pink in a basic solution, so a matches (ii).
(b) CuO dissolves in HCl and forms blue-green CuCl2, so b matches (i).
(c) CO2 reacts with Ca(OH)2 to form insoluble white CaCO3, which makes the lime water milky. So c matches (iii).
(d) Zinc displaces hydrogen from the acid, and hydrogen burns with a pop sound. So d matches (iv).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: When carbon dioxide is passed through lime water, the solution first turns milky, but the milkiness disappears if excess carbon dioxide is passed.
Statement II: Calcium carbonate reacts with water and carbon dioxide to form calcium hydrogencarbonate, which is soluble in water.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both statements are true, and Statement II explains Statement I.
Both statements are true, but Statement II does not explain Statement I.
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation:
First, CO$_2$ reacts with lime water to form insoluble $CaCO_3$, which appears as a white precipitate (milkiness).
With excess CO$_2$, this happens: $CaCO_3 + H_2O + CO_2 \rightarrow Ca(HCO_3)_2$, which is soluble in water.
The precipitate dissolves, so the milkiness disappears.
Both statements are true, and Statement II gives the reason for Statement I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Match the substances in List-I with their approximate pH values in List-II.
List-I
(a) 1 M HCl
(b) Lemon juice
(c) Human blood
(d) 1 M NaOH
List-II
(p) about 7.4
(q) about 14
(r) about 0
(s) about 2.2
questions.explanation:
(a) 1 M HCl is a strong acid and gives a very high H$^+$ concentration, so its pH is about 0. This gives (r).
(b) Lemon juice is acidic but weaker than 1 M HCl, with a pH of about 2.2. This gives (s).
(c) Blood is slightly basic, about 7.4, which lies within the body's working range of 7.0 to 7.8. This gives (p).
(d) 1 M NaOH is a strong alkali, so its pH is about 14. This gives (q).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following salts give an aqueous solution with pH less than 7?
$NaCl$, $AlCl_3$, $ZnSO_4$, $CuSO_4$, $Na_2CO_3$, $NH_4Cl$, $KNO_3$, $CH_3COONa$
questions.explanation:
A pH below 7 means the salt comes from a strong acid and a weak base.
Acidic salts:
$AlCl_3$ ($HCl$ + $Al(OH)_3$), $ZnSO_4$ ($H_2SO_4$ + $Zn(OH)_2$), $CuSO_4$ ($H_2SO_4$ + $Cu(OH)_2$) and $NH_4Cl$ ($HCl$ + $NH_4OH$).
Neutral salts (strong acid + strong base): $NaCl$ and $KNO_3$.
Basic salts (strong base + weak acid): $Na_2CO_3$ and $CH_3COONa$.
So 4 of the salts are acidic.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Riya takes 2 mL of dilute NaOH solution in a test tube and adds two drops of phenolphthalein. She then adds dilute HCl drop by drop until a colour change occurs. Finally, she adds a few drops of NaOH to the mixture. How many of the following statements about her observations are correct?
(i) The solution is pink at the start because NaOH is basic.
(ii) The pink colour disappears once the added HCl has neutralised the NaOH.
(iii) At the moment the solution turns colourless, it still contains a large excess of NaOH.
(iv) The pink colour reappears at the end because the mixture becomes basic again.
(v) The NaCl formed in the reaction turns phenolphthalein pink.
(vi) The neutralisation can be shown as $H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l)$.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: phenolphthalein is pink in a basic solution.
(ii) Correct: HCl neutralises the base, so the pink colour is discharged.
(iii) Incorrect: the colour vanishes because the base has been neutralised. A large excess of NaOH would keep the solution pink.
(iv) Correct: the added NaOH makes the mixture basic again, so pink returns.
(v) Incorrect: NaCl comes from a strong acid and a strong base, so it is neutral and does not turn phenolphthalein pink.
(vi) Correct: this is the net neutralisation reaction.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Case: Two students each mix 5 mL of concentrated sulphuric acid with 50 mL of water.
Student P pours the water quickly into a beaker containing the acid.
Student Q adds the acid drop by drop into the water while stirring.
Which conclusion is correct?
options: Q's method releases much less heat in total, which is why it is safer
Both methods are equally safe because the total heat released is about the same

The final solutions have the same $H_3O^+$ concentration, but in P's method the first small amount of water is heated intensely by a large amount of acid, which can cause splashing or cracking of the glass
P's final solution has a lower $H_3O^+$ concentration because water added to acid dilutes it more
questions.explanation:
Both students use the same amounts of acid and water, so the final dilution and $H_3O^+$ concentration are the same.
The total heat released is also about the same. The danger comes from where that heat is released.
In P's method, a little water meets a large amount of acid, so heat builds up locally. The mixture may splash or the glass may crack.
In Q's method, each drop of acid meets a large volume of water with stirring, so the heat spreads out.
Options (1), (2) and (4) each ignore local heating or wrongly claim the concentrations differ.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Complete the general word equation:
Metal hydrogencarbonate + Acid → Salt + ______ + ______
options: Hydrogen gas + Water
Carbon dioxide + Hydrogen gas
Carbon dioxide + Water
Oxygen + Water
questions.explanation:
All metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water.
Example: NaHCO$_3$ + HCl → NaCl + H$_2$O + CO$_2$.
Hydrogen gas is the product of an acid reacting with a metal, so options with H$_2$ are wrong.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A solution of pH 3 is more acidic than a solution of pH 5.
Reason (R): The higher the hydronium ion concentration, the lower the pH value.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. pH 3 lies further below 7 than pH 5, so that solution is more acidic.
R is true. NCERT states that higher [H$_3$O$^+$] means lower pH.
A lower pH means more H$_3$O$^+$ ions, which is exactly why the pH 3 solution is more acidic. So R explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Fresh milk has a pH of about 6. A milkman adds a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk. Which option correctly describes the effect on the pH of the milk and on its setting into curd?
options: pH falls below 6 and the milk sets into curd faster
pH becomes slightly alkaline and the milk takes longer to set, because the lactic acid formed is first neutralised
pH becomes slightly alkaline and the milk sets faster, because a base speeds up curd formation
pH stays at 6 because baking soda is a neutral salt, so setting time is unchanged
questions.explanation:
Baking soda (NaHCO$_3$) is a mild basic salt. Adding it shifts the milk's pH from 6 to slightly alkaline.
When milk turns into curd, lactic acid is formed and the pH falls.
In treated milk, the lactic acid produced must first neutralise the added baking soda before the pH can drop enough for curd to form. So setting is delayed.
Baking soda is not neutral, which rules out option (4).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
How many of the following are uses of bleaching powder according to NCERT?
(i) Bleaching cotton and linen in the textile industry
(ii) Bleaching wood pulp in paper factories
(iii) As an oxidising agent in chemical industries
(iv) Making drinking water free from germs
(v) Removing permanent hardness of water
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: it bleaches cotton and linen.
(ii) Correct: it bleaches wood pulp in paper factories.
(iii) Correct: it is used as an oxidising agent.
(iv) Correct: it disinfects drinking water.
(v) Incorrect: washing soda, not bleaching powder, removes permanent hardness.
So 4 of the uses are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Two test tubes X and Y each contain an equal length of magnesium ribbon. Equal volumes of two different acids of the same molar concentration are added, one to each tube. Fizzing in X is vigorous, while in Y it is slow. Which conclusion is correct?
options: The acid in Y is a strong acid, so it reacts slowly to produce more hydrogen.
The acid in X produces more H$^+$ ions, so it has a lower pH than the acid in Y.
The acid in X has a higher pH because it releases hydrogen gas faster.
Both acids have the same pH because their concentrations are equal.
questions.explanation:
The fizzing is hydrogen gas formed when the acid reacts with Mg.
The rate depends on the H$^+$ ions available, so vigorous fizzing in X means its acid gives more H$^+$. X behaves like HCl, and Y like acetic acid.
More H$^+$ means a lower pH, so X has the lower pH.
Option 4 fails because equal concentration does not mean equal pH: strong and weak acids ionise to different extents.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
How many of the following are uses of washing soda?
Glass industry, soap industry, antacid tablets, paper industry, manufacture of borax, baking powder, removing permanent hardness of water
questions.explanation:
Washing soda is used in the glass, soap and paper industries. That makes 3.
It is used to manufacture borax. That makes 4.
It removes permanent hardness of water. That makes 5.
Antacid tablets and baking powder are uses of baking soda, not washing soda.
Total = 5.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: In an equation for an acid in water, the hydrogen ion may be written simply as a free, independent $H^+$ ion. There is no need to show its association with water.
Statement II: When any acid is neutralised by any base in aqueous solution, the essential reaction is $H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l)$.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Hydrogen ions cannot exist alone. They combine with water and must be shown as H+(aq) or $H_3O^+$.
Statement II is correct. All acids give H+(aq) and all bases give $OH^-(aq)$ in water.
Writing $HX + MOH \rightarrow MX + HOH$ in ionic form reduces to $H^+(aq) + OH^-(aq) \rightarrow H_2O(l)$.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A white sodium compound X is used in antacids and in soda-acid fire extinguishers. On heating, X gives a solid Y, water, and a gas that turns lime water milky. When Y is recrystallised from water, it gives a crystalline salt Z. Which of the following is correct?
options: X is $Na_2CO_3$, Y is $NaOH$, and Z is used to bleach cotton.
X is $NaHCO_3$, Y is $NaOH$, and Z is $Na_2CO_3.10H_2O$.
X is $NaHCO_3$, Y is $Na_2CO_3$, and Z is used to make baking powder.
X is $NaHCO_3$, Y is $Na_2CO_3$, and Z is used to remove permanent hardness of water.
questions.explanation:
X is used in antacids and fire extinguishers, so X is baking soda, $NaHCO_3$.
On heating: $2NaHCO_3 \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2$. So Y is $Na_2CO_3$, and the gas is CO$_2$, which turns lime water milky.
Recrystallising $Na_2CO_3$ gives washing soda, $Na_2CO_3.10H_2O$ (Z), which is used to remove permanent hardness.
Option (3) fails because baking powder is made from baking soda (X), not from Z.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The formula of Plaster of Paris is written as $CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$. The best explanation for showing half a water molecule is that
options: each water molecule splits into two halves inside the crystal
two formula units of $CaSO_4$ share one molecule of water
only half of the $CaSO_4$ units in the sample contain any water
half of the water evaporates every time the powder is exposed to air
questions.explanation:
A water molecule cannot be split into halves.
NCERT explains that in Plaster of Paris, two formula units of $CaSO_4$ share one water molecule. This makes ½ molecule per formula unit on average.
Option (3) is tempting, but it does not describe a fixed, uniform composition. The ½ is a ratio across formula units, not a description of only some units being hydrated.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 · Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Statement I: Hydrochloric acid and acetic acid of the same concentration (say 1 M) produce different amounts of H$^+$ ions in water.
Statement II: Acetic acid is a strong acid because it gives more H$^+$ ions than hydrochloric acid at the same concentration.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that 1 M HCl and 1 M CH$_3$COOH give different amounts of H$^+$.
Statement II is incorrect. HCl gives more H$^+$ ions, so HCl is the strong acid.
Acetic acid gives fewer H$^+$ ions, so it is a weak acid.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Curd and other sour substances should not be stored in brass or copper vessels because:
options: Curd is basic and dissolves the metal surface
The acid in curd reacts with the metal and forms harmful compounds that contaminate the food
Copper and brass absorb water from curd and make it dry
The metal neutralises the curd and turns it back into milk
questions.explanation:
Curd contains lactic acid, so it is acidic, not basic. This rules out option (1).
Acids react with metals such as copper and with the zinc in brass. The compounds formed are harmful and spoil the food.
Neutralisation needs a base, not a metal, and curd cannot change back into milk. So option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Science
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Crystals of copper sulphate appear dry even though they contain water.
Reason (R): Water of crystallisation is a fixed number of water molecules that forms part of one formula unit of the salt.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true. Copper sulphate crystals look and feel dry, yet heating them releases water.
R is true. This water is a fixed number of molecules (5 for $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$) built into each formula unit.
The water is part of the crystal structure and is not present as free liquid on the surface. That is why the crystals are not wet, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
